subtopics.title: Two Kinds of Scale and What They Promise

questions.question: On a plan drawn to 1 : 50, one centimetre on the page represents:
Why does a bar scale stay correct on a photocopied or resized plan when the ratio does not?
options: The bar scale is printed on the page, so it shrinks or stretches with the drawing
Bar scales are always drawn larger than needed
The bar scale ignores the units used

questions.question: On a road map at 1 : 2 000 000, one centimetre represents:
Comparing 1 : 50 and 1 : 100 for the same page size:
options: 1 : 100 shows more detail because the number is bigger
1 : 50 shows more detail; the bigger the second number, the smaller the drawing relative to reality
1 : 100 can only be used for maps

subtopics.title: From Ruler to Reality — and Back

questions.question: A wall measures 8,4 cm on a 1 : 50 plan. Its real length is:
A 5,5 m stoep drawn at 1 : 100 appears on the page as a line of:
Carpet for a 4,20 m by 3,00 m room at R189,00 per m² costs:
An 11 m² stoep is paved with blocks 0,2 m by 0,1 m, plus 5% for breakage. Blocks needed:
A floor plan is a view:
options: From directly above, as though the roof were lifted off
From an angle, showing three sides at once
From the front, standing on the lawn
Along the length of the passage

questions.question: The quarter-circle arc drawn across a gap in a wall shows:
A dimension of 4 200 written on a builder's floor plan usually means:
Which answer about a layout would earn the most marks?
options: The plan shows a bedroom, a bathroom and a kitchen
Move the door to the opposite side of the wall so it opens against the wall instead of into the passage
The plan is drawn to scale

subtopics.title: Elevation Plans and What They Add

questions.question: An elevation plan shows:
options: The arrangement of rooms and how they connect
The floor area of each room
Wall heights, the roof shape and the vertical position of windows

questions.question: The 'north elevation' of a house is:
options: The side of the house that faces north
The northern half of the floor plan
The wall with the north arrow drawn on it

questions.question: With a perimeter of 14,4 m from the plan and a height of 2,4 m from the elevation, the gross wall area is:
After deducting a door of 1,89 m² and a window of 1,44 m², the wall area to be plastered is:
To go from a measurement on the page to the real measurement, you:
A 6,0 cm line on a 1 : 50 plan represents a wall of:
Reading '1 : 100' as a shrinking factor means the drawing is:
options: One hundred times larger than reality
One hundred times smaller than reality

subtopics.title: The Bird's Eye and the Standing-in-Front View

questions.question: Which question can ONLY be answered by the elevation?
options: How big is the bedroom floor?
How high above the floor does the window sill sit?
Does the door open into the passage?
Is the kitchen next to the dining area?

questions.question: On a floor plan, a thin triple line in a wall represents:
The elevation is described as which kind of view?
options: A view from an angle showing depth
The bird's-eye view with the roof removed
A cut-away view through the middle of the house
The standing-in-front view, looking straight at one wall

questions.question: Why does the north arrow on a floor plan matter to a family?
options: It shows which way the plan should be filed
It sets the scale of the drawing
It tells them which rooms will get sun and which face the weather

subtopics.title: Turning the Plan into a Shopping List

questions.question: Skirting board for the 4,20 m by 3,00 m room, less a 0,9 m doorway, at R42,00/m costs:
Carpet uses area and skirting uses perimeter because:
options: Carpet covers the floor surface, while skirting runs around its edge
Carpet is sold in rolls and skirting in boxes
Perimeter is always cheaper to calculate
Skirting is measured in square metres too

questions.question: Each paving block is 0,2 m by 0,1 m, so it covers:
The wall-area calculation needs both drawings because:
options: Every exam question requires two sources
The plan gives the walk-around distance and the elevation gives the height
The elevation is drawn at a different scale
The plan cannot be measured accurately
